primitives.description:
A small drawing that moves, for something happening now: loading, a call that is live, somebody
typing, somebody speaking.

`name` picks the drawing:

- `spinner` — a turning ring, for waiting on something.
- `live` — a dot with a ring going out from it, for something running now: a live call, a
  recording (in the danger tone), somebody online.
- `typing` — three dots rising in turn, for somebody writing, or the assistant thinking.
- `speaking` — bars moving out of step, for whoever is talking, or audio playing.

Sized and coloured as `we-icon` is, so one can take an icon's place: `size` is a size token or any
CSS length, and with none it is the icon size its container publishes. Its colour is the accent
unless `color` names a role, a palette token or any CSS colour — so `tone` re-points it, a live
dot inside a success badge is the success colour, and `color: 'currentColor'` makes it the text's.

Every copy of a drawing is at the same point in its cycle at the same moment, wherever and
whenever it mounted: the live dots in a sidebar and on a page pulse together, and a spinner that
reappears after the window reloads picks up where the last left off.

For somebody who asked for less motion, the dot and the bars stand still, the typing dots fade in
turn rather than rise, and the spinner keeps turning, since a still spinner looks stuck.
A colour, chosen from the theme's tokens or picked by hand.

Makes whatever is inside it something that can be picked up and carried somewhere else.

## Why this exists as a primitive

A post card, a member row and a space in the sidebar are rendered by **templates**, which are
data. If making one draggable were a code change, every future draggable surface would be a code
change too, and the contribution ladder says arrangement stays data. This is the same rung
`we-sortable` occupies: two custom elements and an existing `$invoke`, with no new prop resolver,
no new operator, and nothing added to the expression grammar.

```json
{ "type": "we-draggable",
  "props": { "entity": "CollectionBlock", "recordId": { "$": "post.id" }, "label": { "$": "post.title" } },
  "children": [ "…the card…" ] }
```

## What it carries

A **reference** — `{ dataset?, entity, id }` — never DOM, and never the row object. `dataset` is
deliberately left empty here: a card fragment cannot name its own dataset without reading a
store, and portable fragments name no store by construction. The receiver stamps it, from
whichever dataset was current when the drop happened.

## Text inside it stays selectable

A press on the words of a rendered composition — anything inside a `data-we-text` region — selects
them rather than picking the card up. The rest of the card, including the space around those
words, still drags. See `shared/textHit.ts`.

## Nesting

A draggable inside a draggable is how a picture is taken out of a post rather than the whole post:
the innermost one under the press claims it, and the outer one sees the claim and stands aside.

## `display: contents`

The wrapper must not exist as a box. A card inside a grid track, a row inside a flex column: a
real element in between would take the track and leave the card laid out against the wrapper
instead of the grid. What is dragged is therefore the *child*, which is also what the ghost and
the geometry are measured from.

primitives.description:
Anything a `we-draggable` can be dropped into.

The receiving half of the pair, and the same rung: two custom elements and an existing `$invoke`,
so a template can make a region a drop target without a code change.

```json
{ "type": "we-drop-zone",
  "props": { "accepts": "CollectionBlock,Space,Agent",
             "onDropped": { "$invoke": "modules.pocket.gather", "args": [{ "$": "event.detail" }] } },
  "children": [ "…the panel…" ] }
```

## It emits intent, it never mutates

Exactly `we-sortable`'s rule, and for the same reason: what a drop *means* differs. A panel writes
a record, a composer inserts a block, a board records a position. A primitive that assumed one of
those would be useless to the others.

## `accepts` is a list of entity names, as a string

A comma-separated string rather than an array because that is what an HTML attribute is, and
because a schema writing `"accepts": "CollectionBlock,Space"` needs no expression. Empty means
"anything", which is right for a general-purpose tray and wrong for a composer — say what you
take.

## Zones nest, and the innermost one wins

A folder inside a panel, a card inside a board. Hit-testing picks the innermost accepting zone
and fires exactly one drop — and these events **do not bubble**, so that decision survives the
DOM. See `_zone` for what happened when they did.

Give every nested zone `noArm`, so picking something up speaks once about the container rather
than once about every row inside it.

Renders a raw HTML string safely via DOMPurify sanitization.

Use this instead of `we-text` when content is stored as HTML (e.g. rich-text
editor output such as Flux messages). The `content` prop accepts any HTML
fragment; it is sanitized before rendering so XSS payloads are stripped.

## SVG animation: CSS keyframes, not SMIL

Inline SVG passes through, and so does animation written as CSS — a `<style>` block with
`@keyframes` inside the SVG, or a `<animateMotion>` following a path. **A SMIL `<animate>` or
`<set>` element does not**: DOMPurify's default allowlist excludes them, so they are removed and
the drawing renders static.

That exclusion is deliberate and stays. `<set attributeName="href" to="javascript:…">` is a real
XSS vector against an `<a>`, which is precisely the shape of payload this element exists to
strip — and SMIL is a dead end besides, deprecated in spirit and unevenly implemented, where CSS
animation is neither.

What was wrong was not the policy but the silence: an author wrote something reasonable, it
typechecked, it validated, and it did nothing, with no diagnostic anywhere. warnAboutSmil
is the diagnostic. It says what was dropped and what to write instead, once per element, in
development only.

Vertical list container for menu items inside a popover.
Not a standalone selector — wrap in we-popover for dropdown behavior.

Single actionable item inside a we-menu.
Supports selected and active states; `tone: 'danger'` marks a destructive item.

Low-level floating panel anchored to a trigger element.
Use DropdownMenu component for dropdown menus.

A drag target that reports how far it has moved, and nothing else.

## Why it reports a delta rather than owning a size

The obvious design is a handle that resizes its neighbour. It is the wrong one, because "what does
this drag mean" is never the handle's business: the editor's panel rails grow *leftwards* from a
width that starts at zero when the panel is closed, clamp at a minimum, and close the panel again
below a threshold — while a docked call panel grows from whichever edge it is attached to. A
handle that owned the size could serve one of those and not the other.

So it emits `resizestart`, `resize` and `resizeend`, each carrying `delta`: pixels moved along its
axis **since the drag began**, signed in screen direction (right and down positive). The consumer
captures its own starting size and applies whatever sign and limits it has. Delta-from-start
rather than incremental, because every consumer would otherwise have to accumulate, and one of
them would get it wrong after a dropped event.

## Why a primitive rather than a hook

There were two implementations of this before it existed and they diverged in ways nobody chose:
the editor's is mouse-only, so it does not work on a touchscreen at all, and its rail is a plain
div — not focusable, so there is no way to resize a panel from the keyboard. Pointer events and a
`separator` role fix both once, for every consumer, in the layer where imperative DOM work belongs.

Pick a single value from a list of options. Custom-rendered dropdown.
Use for form fields, settings, filters. Set searchable=true for type-to-filter.

A drop zone whose items can be picked up, reordered, and moved to other zones.

## One element, not two

A zone *is* the container and its children *are* the items, which is what makes nesting free: a
sortable inside an item of another sortable is simply a zone inside a zone, with no special case
anywhere. A separate `we-drag-item` would buy nothing and cost boilerplate at every call site.

## It emits intent, it never mutates

A drop fires SortableMoveDetail — "this item moved from there to here, at this index" —
and nothing else. What that *means* is the consumer's business, and it differs: a kanban route
keyed on `status` writes a scalar, a board built from containment relinks two `children` edges, an
outline reparents a node. A primitive that assumed one of those would be useless to the others.

This is also why the element does not reorder its own DOM. The list is rendered from data; the
data changes; the list re-renders. A primitive that moved nodes itself would fight whatever
renders them.

## Nesting, and why cycles are not a problem

The hard part of nested drag-and-drop is refusing to drop a container into its own descendant.
Because nesting here is expressed *in the DOM*, that check is `dragged.contains(zone)` — correct
by construction, needing no knowledge of the consumer's data shape. The innermost matching zone
under the pointer wins, so dropping into a nested list does not also count as dropping into its
parent.

## A zone that can be empty needs a size

Hit-testing is by the zone's own bounding rectangle, so a zone holding nothing is a zero-height
rectangle and nothing can be dropped into it — which is precisely the zone a person most wants to
drop into. **Give any zone that can empty a `flex` or a `minHeight`**; without one the surrounding
box may look like the target while not being it, which is worse than looking undroppable.

Left to the consumer rather than defaulted here, because how much room an empty list should hold
is a design decision and differs per surface — a kanban column reserves a trough, a reorderable
settings list should collapse. What the primitive owes is that the rule is written down where
somebody wiring one up will read it.

## Keyboard

Space or Enter picks up the focused item; the arrow keys move it, along the list and across
zones; Space drops and Escape cancels. Built in rather than added later, because a board that can
only be operated by dragging is a board some people cannot operate at all — and because the
events are identical, a consumer gets it for nothing.

## Items that contain form controls: `[data-we-handle]`

By default the whole item is the grab area, which is right for a card or a nav row. It is wrong
the moment an item contains a text field: dragging to select text would start a drag, and — worse
— the keyboard pickup would read a **space typed into an input** as "pick this up", so the field
could not accept spaces at all.

So two rules, both no-ops for an item without form controls:

- Mark one or more descendants `data-we-handle`, and only a press that begins inside a handle
  starts a drag. An item with no handle keeps dragging from anywhere, so existing consumers are
  unaffected.
- A Space or Enter that originates in a text-entry element (`input`, `textarea`, `select`,
  `contenteditable`, including inside a component's shadow root) is typing, never a pickup. This
  applies whether or not the item declares handles, because an unfocusable-by-design input that
  swallows spaces is a bug in every consumer that could hit it.

Make the handle itself focusable (a `we-button` will do) so the keyboard path stays open: Space
on a focused handle picks the row up exactly as it does on a plain item.

## Overlays opened from an item are not part of it

A press that begins inside an `OverlayElement` — a modal, a drawer, a popover — never drags the
item that overlay happens to sit inside, and no consumer has to declare anything for that.

It is worth knowing why the case exists at all. A modal opened from a row is usually *declared* in
that row, because it needs the row's data to say what it is renaming; overlays are promoted to the
browser's top layer rather than reparented, so the sheet paints above the whole page while DOM
containment still says it is inside the row. Without this rule, dragging to select text in a rename
field dragged the column behind the modal.

Same principle as nested zones, one layer up: the innermost thing under the pointer owns the
gesture. A sortable *inside* an overlay is unaffected — only the path between the press and the
item is considered.

Displays a formatted or relative timestamp that self-updates each minute
when `relative` is enabled.

A tree — the space as a file browser, a folder list, an outline. The root of one, holding its items.

## One root, items to any depth

The data a tree shows is usually fractal (a channel holds channels), and so is `we-tree-item`: an
item's children are more items, nested inside it. The widget is not: there is exactly one
`we-tree`, because ARIA allows one `tree` per widget and the keyboard treats every visible row as a
single list. Arrow-down from the last row of a sub-channel lands on its parent's next sibling, and
Tab enters and leaves the tree once. A `we-tree` per level would make every subtree its own tab stop
and its own island of focus, and a screen reader would announce a dozen trees.

## The keyboard

Roving focus: one row is the tab stop, the arrows move it. Down and Up walk the visible rows in
order; Right opens a closed row, or steps into an open one; Left closes an open row, or steps out to
its parent; Home and End go to the ends; Enter and Space select. Typing a letter moves to the next
row whose label starts with it. This is the WAI-ARIA tree pattern, and it lives here, once, so no
template has to write it.

## What it emits, and what it does not decide

`select` — `{ value }` — when a row is chosen, by click or key. What choosing means (navigating,
filtering) is the template's business. Which row is selected is the template's too: pass
`selected` and the matching item marks itself, so a selection driven by the address stays in step.

One row of a `we-tree`, and the rows under it.

The row's own content goes in the default slot — an icon, a label, a badge, a count, whatever the
template arranges (the kit's `treeRow` fragment is the usual one). Rows under it go in the
`children` slot, rendered only while it is open: a template that loads them lazily puts its query
inside an `$if` on the same open state, so nothing is read for a row nobody has opened.

`open` is the template's to hold, as `selected` is the tree's: the row asks (`openchange`, `{ open }`,
bound as `onOpenChange`) and the template answers by setting it, so a row's open state can live in the address, in local
state or anywhere else.

A line whose last part types itself, holds, deletes and types the next phrase — "We are building
a global brain", then "We are building intelligence no one owns".

A primitive because it is behaviour: timers, the reader's motion setting, and what a screen reader
hears are code's to own, and a template has no timers. It takes its type from where it sits, so a
heading's size and weight reach it; put it inside the `we-text` that sets them.

- **Still for anyone who asked for less motion** — the system's setting or the app's. It shows the
  first phrase in full, with no caret, and nothing moves.
- **One sentence to a screen reader.** The fixed part and every phrase, read once; the typing is
  hidden from it, since a sentence rewriting itself a letter at a time is noise.
- **The page under it does not jump.** A hidden copy of the longest phrase holds the line's size.

The first phrase is drawn in full before anything types, so the line reads right at once.

components.name: GraphView
components.description:
A general-purpose graph view: knowledge maps, schema maps, hierarchies, cluster maps and
free-positioned canvases, all from the same engine.

The shape of a graph is set by four independent choices: where it starts (`seeds`), how much of it
opens (`expansion`), how it is arranged (`layout`), and how it looks (`nodeStyle` / `edgeStyle`).

Common recipes:
- **Knowledge map** — `seeds: { source: 'query', options: { entity: 'Belief' } }` with
`expansion: { defaultDepth: 1 }` and `layout: { type: 'force' }`.
- **Schema map** — `seeds: { source: 'schema' }`, which draws the dataset's own entity types and
the relations between them. Picks up model types added later with no template change.
- **Hierarchy** — `layout: { type: 'tree' }` with a `collection` expansion for nested content.
- **Static diagram** — `seeds: { literal: true, nodes: [...], edges: [...] }` and no expansion at all.
- **A canvas with a grid** — `backdrop: { pattern: 'dots', gap: 24 }`, or `'lines'`; it pans and
zooms with the canvas and is coloured from a role (`border` unless `color` says otherwise).

sources.name: arrangedBoard
sources.doc: A board worked out from its three subscriptions — { ready, gathers, columns, contents, unplaced, unplacedStates, available, total, involved, filtering, show, dimmed, cardCount, matchedCount, unplacedTotal, rows, cells, rowCounts, workflow, awaiting, awaitingOnly }. columns are the caller’s own column records in the board’s order; contents[columnId] is { label, icon, color, lane, arranged, unarranged, count, shown, matched, order }; unplaced is work no column here shows. Options: board (the record with children hydrated), columns (its kind: "column" children), records (everything in scope), states (spaceStore.taskStates). To read it by who is on the work, also pass involvements (an Involvement query), kinds (spaceStore.involvementTypes), people (the chosen DIDs), me (me.did — involved is everyone on a card here, the viewer first) and show: "dim" lists the others in dimmed and moves nothing; "hide" drops them from arranged, unarranged and unplaced while count stays true and shown says how many are drawn; "rows" adds a row per person plus "nobody" — rows are keys, cells[row][columnId] is { arranged, unarranged, count }. A drag in a column showing only part of itself passes contents[columnId].order to arrangeColumn, so the hidden cards keep their places. Where the space’s states ask for agreement (spaceStore.taskWorkflowEnabled) a card is drawn where its run is, and three more fields answer: workflow[cardId] is { to, approvers, counted, needs, mine, canApprove, approverKind } for a card waiting on a move — counted is how many of approvers count toward needs; awaiting is the cards whose waiting move the viewer’s approval would help; pass awaitingMe: true to draw only those (awaitingOnly says it is on).
sources.example: arrangedBoard({ board: first(local.board), columns: local.columns, records: local.pool, states: spaceStore.taskStates }).columns

sources.name: involvement
sources.doc: Who is on each record, from the Involvement rows — { byNode, answers, dids }. byNode[recordId] is { people, dids, responsible, reviewing, committed, interested, declined, pairs }: people are { did, kind, name, semantic, reflexive, icon, color, tone }, assignees first then reviewers and so on, and tone is the avatar ring the part wears ("warning" for reviewing, empty otherwise) — pass it as an AvatarStack avatar’s tone; the five lists are DIDs grouped by what each kind means, so a renamed or added kind still lands in the right one; dids is everyone not declined; pairs is every "did|kind" present, for a menu tick with `in`. answers[recordId] is the viewer’s own reflexive answer (going, maybe, …). Options: rows (an Involvement query), types (spaceStore.involvementTypes), me (me.did, who then leads the top-level dids), nodes (record ids the top-level dids is limited to).
sources.example: involvement({ rows: local.involvements, types: spaceStore.involvementTypes, me: me.did }).byNode[card.id].responsible

sources.name: involvementMenu
sources.doc: The entries of a "who is on this" DropdownMenu for one record: the member a conversation named, when `said` matches exactly one and nobody is doing it yet; "Assign to me" while the viewer is not already on it, then a group per kind the entity is offered that anybody may give (the first open, the rest closed unless somebody holds them), each listing members with their faces — current holders ticked and first, then the viewer, then everyone by name. Every entry carries `kind`, and a toggle `checked`, so one handler serves all: setInvolvement(record, arg.id, arg.kind, !arg.checked). Options: node, entity, rows (an Involvement query), types (spaceStore.offeredInvolvementTypes), members (spaceStore.members), profiles (profileStore.profiles), me (me.did), said (a name somebody said — TaskBlock.assignee).
sources.example: involvementMenu({ node: card.id, entity: 'TaskBlock', rows: local.involvements, types: spaceStore.offeredInvolvementTypes, members: spaceStore.members, profiles: profileStore.profiles, me: me.did })

sources.name: signalTally
sources.doc: What a record's reactions say, as one number. With `type`, the number THAT type is read as — a toggle counts, a vote nets out, a rating averages, and a community's own `aggregate` wins unless the mode cannot express it. Without a type, how many people reacted at all: records, never values, since a total summing likes and stars and downvotes is not a number. Retired types still count — somebody reacted, and a total that fell when a vocabulary was tidied would be reporting the tidying. Options: signals (the record's `signals`, hydrated), type (a SignalType row).

sources.name: reactions
sources.doc: A record's reactions with this agent's own newest answer in place, whether or not it has been read back yet. Every reaction surface draws through it: a press writes a record and the subscription answers about a second later, so without it the glyph stays unfilled and the count stays put and the press reads as having failed. The LIST rather than the count, because the tally, the mark and the control all read it — overlay the count alone and the heart sits unfilled beside a number that moved. Options: signals (the record's `signals`, hydrated), record (its id), type (the SignalType's id), me (me.did).
sources.example: reactions({ signals: filter(row.signals, { signalTypeId: sig.id }), record: row.id, type: sig.id, me: me.did })

sources.name: reactors
sources.doc: Who reacted with one type and what each gave — { people, total, unresolved }. `people` are { did, name, avatar, value, mine }, the reader first and then by name; `total` counts everybody before any search, which is what "12 people" says. The record already carries this — `include: { signals: true }` hydrates each Signal's author and value — so nothing is fetched; what a schema cannot do is join a DID to a face and a name. `search` narrows by name, and `unresolved` says how many could not be judged because their profile has not arrived. Options: signals (one type's signals, hydrated), profiles (profileStore.profiles), me (me.did), search.
sources.example: reactors({ signals: filter(row.signals, { signalTypeId: sig.id }), profiles: profileStore.profiles, me: me.did })

sources.name: signalTypesByUse
sources.doc: Reaction types ordered by how many PEOPLE reacted with each, most first — never by what they said, since a total of values cannot compare a rating with a vote and a downvoted type would sort below one nobody has used. Ties keep the order they arrived in, so a panel does not reshuffle as reactions come in. Muted authors are left out of the count. It orders and nothing else: which types a surface draws is a filter, and stays in the schema — which is what keeps an overflow count evaluable, since reordering a list cannot change how long it is. Sorting is here because the expression language has no sort, the grammar is closed, and these types come from a subscription rather than a query that could carry an `order`. Pass `of` — the record's id — and the order SETTLES: it is worked out the first time that record's reactions are drawn and then held, so a reaction somebody withdraws does not slide down the column under their cursor. It has to be held outside the template, because a reaction surface sits inside an `$each` over a query and a subscription hands the renderer fresh objects, which remounts the row and takes any `$localState` with it. Types the settled order has never seen are appended by use, so nothing new is hidden; the order is dropped when the space changes. Options: of (the record whose order this is), types (the rows to order), signals (the record's `signals`, hydrated), muted (spaceStore.mutedDids), limit (keep the first N of that order).
sources.example: signalTypesByUse({ of: row.id, types: local.signalTypes.filter(t, !t.retired), signals: row.signals, muted: spaceStore.mutedDids, limit: 4 })

sources.name: voices

Options: summary (what a GraphView's onSeedSummary reported — the canvas seed's `{ type, voices }`), param (the weights as the address holds them, `did=50,did=0`), profiles (profileStore.profiles), me (me.did).
sources.example: voices({ summary: local.voiceSummary, param: local.voices, profiles: profileStore.profiles, me: me.did })

sources.name: voicesParam

sources.name: formatJson
sources.doc: A JSON string indented for reading, or the text unchanged when it will not parse — which is the case worth showing rather than swallowing. Options: text. For displaying a stored blob (an interpretation pass’s prompt and response); a schema has no JSON.stringify of its own.

sources.name: treeSpines

sources.name: treeSpine
sources.doc: A tree spine as the tree reads it, from the picker's value (local.spine): its kind — any, relationship (with id) or relation (with class and prop for one, without for all) — and selector (the forest layout's spine), offSpine (the when of a rule drawing the other lines faint; absent for any) and relations (whether the canvas seed should draw the models' relations). sources.doc: Whether a model made a record: { by: "run", run } naming the run that wrote it (a transcribed line, a record an interpretation pass or an agent made, a reply in the editor’s chat), or null for what a person made. Reads the record’s own generatedBy, as an id or an included record, so it needs no query. Ask this rather than reading the relation. Options: record.

settings.description: Let people here see each other’s pointers.

settings.label: Driving
settings.description: Let one person take the wheel, so others can follow their screen.

modules.name: Pocket
modules.description: Keep things from any space — posts, people, spaces — in a panel that follows you.

members.name: close
members.doc: Closes the Pocket panel.

members.name: open
members.doc: Whether the Pocket panel is open.

members.name: show
members.doc: Opens the Pocket panel and resolves the folder it was last looking at.

members.name: toggle
members.doc: Opens the Pocket panel, or closes it if it is open.

modules.name: Notes
modules.description: Private notes that follow you between spaces. Share one into a space as a post.

modules.name: Globe
modules.description: A globe with a modular layer system — data on the earth, borders, the sky — drawn by Cesium or MapLibre.

members.name: drawsSpace
members.doc: Whether the globe draws the space around the earth — the skybox, stars and solar system. False on MapLibre.

members.name: engine
members.doc: Which engine draws the globe here — "cesium" or "maplibre" — from the setting and this device.

settings.label: Globe engine
settings.description: What draws the globe. Cesium is the full 3D globe, with the stars and planets around it and lines that arc. MapLibre is lighter and quicker on a phone: the same earth and the same data, with lines drawn flat and nothing around the earth. Automatic uses MapLibre on phones, tablets and small machines, and Cesium everywhere else.

settings.label: Globe imagery
settings.description: What the globe's surface is drawn with. NASA's needs no account and is sharp to about 30 m. The others are sharp to street level and need a key from your own account, set below; using one means accepting that provider's terms. A provider with no key, or a key it refuses, draws NASA's.

settings.label: Cesium ion access token
settings.description: From ion.cesium.com → Access Tokens. Used when the imagery is Cesium ion.

settings.label: Esri API key
settings.description: From developers.arcgis.com → API keys, with the basemap styles privilege. Used when the imagery is Esri World Imagery. Esri serves the imagery even for a key it does not recognise, so check this one carefully: a mistyped key draws the imagery without your account being used.

settings.label: Mapbox access token
settings.description: From account.mapbox.com → Tokens; a public token. Used when the imagery is Mapbox Satellite.

modules.name: Graph
modules.description: A general-purpose graph engine — knowledge maps, schema maps, hierarchies and diagrams, with pluggable expanders, layouts and behaviours.

modules.name: Flux
modules.description: Reads conversations a Flux community keeps, in a space synced in from Flux.

members.name: subgroupMessages
members.doc: The messages in one of Flux’s conversation subgroups, oldest first — { id, author, timestamp, body }. Read when asked, since a subgroup’s messages are not a relation a $query can follow.

modules.name: Polls
modules.description: Ask the space a question and watch the answer arrive.

members.name: lastError
members.doc: Why the last vote could not be recorded, or empty.

members.name: pendingVote
members.doc: This agent’s vote on a poll, written and not yet read back — { author, option }, or nothing. Keyed by poll id.

members.name: revealBeforeVoting
members.doc: Whether a poll shows its counts before this agent has voted — the community’s setting here.

members.name: vote
members.doc: Casts this agent’s vote on a poll, or changes it — one vote per person per poll.

members.name: voting
members.doc: The id of the poll a vote is being written for, or empty.

settings.label: Show counts before voting
settings.description: Whether a poll’s tally is visible to somebody who has not voted yet.

functions.name: tally
functions.doc: Votes counted per choice — { option, count, share, leading }[] — one row per choice the poll offers, in its order, plus a row for any choice a vote names that the poll no longer does. Options: votes (a Vote query), options (the poll’s comma-separated choices), pending (modules.polls.pendingVote[<poll id>] — this agent’s vote written and not yet read back, counted in place of their stored one so the bars move on the press).
functions.example: tally({ votes: local.votes, options: block.options, pending: modules.polls.pendingVote[block.id] })

operations.name: core.addBoardColumn
operations.description: Add a column to a board: bound to a state when a slug is given — work in that state arrives on its own — or a lane of this board’s own when not.

name.description: The column’s heading. Stored only where it differs from its state’s name.

slug.description: The state the column stands for. Omit for a lane.

states.description: The states the community offers, in its own order, each { slug, name }.

operations.name: core.addStateColumn
operations.description: Give a board a column for a state, unless one of its columns is already bound to it — what naming a new state does to the space’s own board.

states.description: The states the community offers, in its own order, each { slug, name }.

operations.name: core.addTaskStateEvidence
operations.description: Add one requirement to what a state asks to be there before work moves into it.

requirement.description: One requirement as the state stores it: { entity, where?, via?, min? }.

operations.name: core.addTaskToColumn
operations.description: Make a task in a column: parented to the collection the board gathers from where there is one, arranged into the column, in the state given.

anchor.description: The collection it belongs to — the call the board gathers from.

arrange.description: Whether to arrange it into the column. False where its state is still to be agreed.

operations.name: core.arrangeColumn
operations.description: Store the order of a column’s cards: the ids given, then whatever the column still holds that they leave out.

column.description: The column (or a board, for what it holds in no column).

ids.description: Card ids, in the order wanted.

operations.name: core.clearPlacements
operations.description: Take a card off a canvas: every placement it has there, so no duplicate puts it back.

operations.name: core.colorCanvasType
operations.description: Colour every card of one kind on a canvas: the canvas’s style for the kind edited, or made where there is none.

color.description: The colour, or the host’s value for none of its own.

create.description: Whether to make a style where there is none. False when clearing.

operations.name: core.colorSpaceType
operations.description: Colour one kind of record in the space’s key: its style edited, or made where there is none, and any duplicate removed.

operations.name: core.composeCard
operations.description: Compose a card onto a canvas: the post, kept wherever the canvas’s content lives, and its placement on the canvas where a point is given.

root.description: The post’s own fields, as core.createPost takes them.

blocks.description: Its blocks, as core.createPost takes them.

home.description: The collection the card is kept in.

canvas.description: The canvas it is placed on.

at.description: Where on the canvas, { x, y }. Without one it is unplaced, in the tray.

operations.name: core.connectRecords
operations.description: Connect two records with a Relationship — of a community-named kind where one is given — and answer with its id.

source.description: The record the connection runs from.

key.description: The connection’s dedup key, from both ends’ titles and its label.

kind.description: The RelationshipType it is one of.

fields.description: Anything else it says — a label, a description.

home.description: A collection to make it inside.

inline.description: Records made inline, each { key, entity, fields }, for the new record’s relations to point at — by the id `inlineRecordId` gives each key.

operations.name: core.createBoard
operations.description: Make a board with a column for each state given, in that order; optionally inside a collection and gathering from a record.

states.description: The slugs of the states to make a column for, in order, each once.

parent.description: A collection to put the board in. Left loose when the collection is not there.

gathers.description: The record the board draws its work from. Omit for a board showing only what is put on it.

operations.name: core.createInvolvementType
operations.description: Name a kind of part somebody can have in a record — “Shepherd”, “Second pair of eyes” — refused when the space already has one by that name. Whether it is somebody’s own answer is fixed here.

semantic.description: What it means, one of ['responsible', 'reviewing', 'committed', 'interested', 'declined']; responsible otherwise.

reflexive.description: An answer only its own agent gives, rather than something said about them.

appliesTo.description: The entities it is offered on, comma-separated; empty for all.

operations.name: core.createPost
operations.description: Write a composed document — a post, a message or a reply — with its blocks, in a collection or in response to a record, threaded under its subject.

root.description: The root’s own fields: kind, mode, and what it stores about its blocks (editorState, textContent), plus where a copy came from.

blocks.description: The blocks in document order, each { key, entity, fields, parent } — parent the planned id of the collection block it is in, absent at the top level.

container.description: The collection it is a child of.

thread.description: The subject of the thread it joins — respondsTo, or the first record above it that is not itself a response.

generatedBy.description: The ModelRun that wrote it, when a model did.

operations.name: core.createRecord
operations.description: Make one record of any type, with its relations and any records made inline for them, inside a collection where one is named — and answer with its id.

inline.description: Records made inline, each { key, entity, fields }, for the new record’s relations to point at — by the id `inlineRecordId` gives each key.

fields.description: Its fields, relations among them as lists of ids (a to-one as a one-element list).

home.description: The collection it is made inside.

operations.name: core.createRecords
operations.description: Make several records of any type at once, each keyed so its id is known before it is written.

operations.name: core.createRelationshipType
operations.description: Name a kind of connection between two records, refused when the space already has one by that name.

slug.description: The identifier everything holding it stores. Derived from the name when not given.

inverseName.description: What it is called read from the other end.

operations.name: core.createSignalType
operations.description: Name a kind of reaction members can give. A toggle runs 0 to 1 and a vote −1 to 1 whatever is asked, and each mode is read as one number its own way unless told otherwise.

slug.description: The identifier everything holding it stores. Derived from the name when not given.

iconSecondary.description: The glyph for the other end of a vote or a range.

aggregate.description: count, mean, sum or median; the mode’s own when not given.

operations.name: core.createTaskState
operations.description: Name a state this community’s work moves through, refused when the space already has one by that name.

semantic.description: What it counts as, one of ['open', 'active', 'blocked', 'done', 'cancelled']; open when not given.

operations.name: core.deleteRecords
operations.description: Delete several records of any type, for everyone, as one act. Not undoable.

operations.name: core.detachConnection
operations.description: Delete a connection nobody has said anything about. One carrying comments or reactions is refused — select the line itself to remove an argued claim.

operations.name: core.editRecord
operations.description: Change the named fields of one record of any type, leaving the rest — a relation among them as a list of ids, a to-one as one, and a field cleared by giving it no value.

operations.name: core.ensureBoardFor
operations.description: Give a collection a board once it holds a task, and not before; answers with the board’s id, or nothing while it holds no task.

states.description: The slugs a new board gets a column for, in order.

operations.name: core.makeSpaceBoard
operations.description: Make the space’s own board — gathering from the space collection, or from the space where it has none — and name it the space’s board landmark.

root.description: The space collection’s id, where the space has one.

title.description: What the board is called; "Everything" when omitted.

states.description: The slugs to make a column for, in order.

operations.name: core.makeSpaceCollection
operations.description: Make the one collection everything top-level in a new space hangs off, and name it the space’s own. A space that has one keeps it.

autoExtract.description: Whether it is interpreted as it grows.

operations.name: core.markRead
operations.description: Say the invoker has read a record as of now: one marker per record, moved forward.

operations.name: core.moveCard
operations.description: Move a card from one column to another, in one transaction: it leaves the first, joins the second (where it was dropped, or at the end), and takes the second’s state when that column is bound to one.

ids.description: The joined column’s order with the card where it was dropped. Omit to append.

operations.name: core.moveUnder
operations.description: Move a record from one holder to another through a to-many relation the holders declare — off the old list and onto the new in one write, so nobody reads it on neither or on both.

to.description: The holder it joins; absent to take it off and put it nowhere.

operations.name: core.openBoardFor
operations.description: The board a collection points at, made — gathering from the collection, inside it — when it has none yet. Answers with its id, or nothing when the collection is not there.

anchor.description: The collection whose board this is.

title.description: What a board made here is called; "This call" when omitted.

states.description: The slugs a new board gets a column for, in order.

operations.name: core.placeCard
operations.description: Write where a card sits on a canvas, or how it looks there: the placement the canvas draws is edited, or one made where there is none, and duplicates beside it removed. Answers { from, to } — what the fields held before — for an undo.

nodeType.description: Its entity, for a placement made here.

fields.description: Placement fields — x and y, a size, a colour, a rank …

placement.description: The placement the canvas draws for the card, where it has one.

duplicates.description: Placements of the card the drawn one outranks, to remove.

create.description: Whether a card with no placement may be given one. False for a style, which needs a position.

operations.name: core.rankCards
operations.description: Write the ranks that order cards among their siblings in a tree read as arranged, all at once, so the tree never reads a half-written row.

ranks.description: Each { placement, rank }: the placement the canvas draws for a card, and its new rank.

operations.name: core.rekeyConnection
operations.description: Bring a connection’s dedup key back in line with its ends’ titles and its label.

key.description: The key as it should read.

operations.name: core.removeBoardColumn
operations.description: Take a column off a board — never the work in it: its cards move to the board’s own arrangement, so a made board keeps them.

operations.name: core.removeTaskStateEvidence
operations.description: Take one requirement, by its position, out of what a state asks to be there first.

index.description: Its position in the list, from 0.

operations.name: core.renameBoardColumn
operations.description: Rename a column on its board. The state it stands for is untouched; renamed back to the state’s own name, it follows the vocabulary again.

states.description: The states the community offers, in its own order, each { slug, name }.

operations.name: core.reorderBoardColumns
operations.description: Put a board’s columns in an order. Only ids the board already holds are written; any it holds that the order leaves out follow.

ids.description: Column ids, in the order wanted.

operations.name: core.reorderTaskStates
operations.description: Set the order the community reads its states in, by slug. A slug with no record is left out.

slugs.description: The states’ slugs, in the order wanted.

operations.name: core.reorderViews
operations.description: Put the space’s sections in a new order. Only reorders: a section not already on is left off.

order.description: The section ids, in the order wanted.

fallback.description: What the space has while its community has not decided — written whole by the first change, so later defaults do not join a space that has.

operations.name: core.respond
operations.description: Give the invoker’s own answer to a record — going, maybe, not going — replacing any answer they gave before; with no kind, withdraw it.

kind.description: A reflexive InvolvementType’s slug; absent withdraws the answer.

operations.name: core.restyleSpaceType
operations.description: Say how the space presents one kind of record, whole: its styles removed and one made holding exactly the fields given — none, where nothing is left to say.

fields.description: color, display, controls, authoring — what it says.

operations.name: core.retargetConnection
operations.description: Move one end of a connection onto a different record — the claim changes, on every canvas — with its key kept in step with the ends.

node.description: The record the end moves to.

key.description: The connection’s key with the end moved.

operations.name: core.setAgentMuted
operations.description: Mute an account for the invoker everywhere, or unmute it: one record per account while muted, none after.

description.description: Why, for the invoker’s own list.

operations.name: core.setCollectionInterpretation
operations.description: Change what one collection is interpreted for, for everyone in it: whether as it grows, and one model in or out of what it looks for.

autoExtract.description: Interpreted as it grows, or not; absent leaves it.

entity.description: A model to add or remove; absent leaves the list.

fallback.description: What the collection looks for while it holds no list of its own.

operations.name: core.setInvolvement
operations.description: Put somebody on a record as one of the space’s kinds of involvement, or take them off. A kind that is somebody’s own answer is given only by them, and replaces their last.

on.description: The state wanted, so pressing twice cannot undo itself.

operations.name: core.setInvolvementTypeRetired
operations.description: Withdraw a kind of involvement from use, or bring it back, leaving everybody already holding it as they are.

retired.description: Withdrawn from use, or brought back.

operations.name: core.setModuleEnabled
operations.description: Turn a module on or off for the whole space.

fallback.description: What the space has while its community has not decided — written whole by the first change, so later defaults do not join a space that has.

operations.name: core.setModuleVisible
operations.description: Show or hide a module for the invoker only, in one space.

operations.name: core.setMyModuleSetting
operations.description: Write, or withdraw, the invoker’s own answer to one setting in one space.

group.description: The module or capability the setting belongs to.

value.description: The answer; absent withdraws it, so the level has no opinion again.

operations.name: core.setSpaceModuleSetting
operations.description: Write, or withdraw, the community’s answer to one setting.

group.description: The module or capability the setting belongs to.

value.description: The answer; absent withdraws it, so the level has no opinion again.

operations.name: core.setSpaceTemplateOverride
operations.description: Choose the template the invoker sees in one space, over the space’s default.

template.description: A template id, or the value that follows the space.

operations.name: core.setSpaceThemeOverride
operations.description: Choose the theme the invoker sees in one space, over the space’s default.

theme.description: A theme id, or the value that follows the space.

operations.name: core.setTaskStateRetired
operations.description: Withdraw a state from use, or bring it back, leaving the work in it as it is.

retired.description: Withdrawn from use, or brought back.

operations.name: core.setViewEnabled
operations.description: Add a section to the space, at the end, or take it out — for every member. Sections this host does not know stay where they are.

fallback.description: What the space has while its community has not decided — written whole by the first change, so later defaults do not join a space that has.

operations.name: core.setViewVisible
operations.description: Show or hide one of a space’s sections for the invoker only.

operations.name: core.setWorkflowArchived
operations.description: Put a workflow away, or bring it back: the records in it still show and can still finish.

operations.name: core.thread
operations.description: Link a response from the subject of the thread it joins, so the whole discussion under a record is one read.

thread.description: The subject of the thread it joins — what it answers, or the first record above that is not itself a response.

operations.name: core.updateInvolvementType
operations.description: Change a kind of involvement — its name, glyph, colour, meaning and where it is offered. The slug stays, and so does whether it is an answer.

name.description: A new name; empty or absent keeps the old one.

semantic.description: One of ['responsible', 'reviewing', 'committed', 'interested', 'declined']; anything else is ignored.

appliesTo.description: The entities it is offered on, comma-separated; empty for all.

operations.name: core.updateSpaceMeta
operations.description: Change what a space is called and says about itself, whether it is listed, and where it is — a new place replaces the old, and none takes it away.

location.description: { latitude, longitude, name?, city?, country?, countryCode? }, to set the place.

operations.name: core.updateTaskState
operations.description: Change a state the community has — its name, glyph, colour, what it counts as, and what moving into it asks for. The slug stays: it is what every task stores.

name.description: A new name; empty or absent keeps the old one.

semantic.description: What it counts as, one of ['open', 'active', 'blocked', 'done', 'cancelled']; anything else is ignored.

approvals.description: How many must agree to a move into it.

approverKind.description: The involvement kind whose holders’ approval counts; empty for anybody’s.

evidence.description: What must be there first, as the state stores it; empty clears it.

operations.name: core.upsertSignal
operations.description: Give the invoker’s reaction of one type on a record, or change it: one per person per type, edited in place, any duplicates removed.

value.description: What the reaction says. Zero is a value like any other; withdrawing is withdrawSignal.

operations.name: core.withdrawSignal
operations.description: Take back the invoker’s reaction of one type on a record — every copy of it, so a doubled one does not survive the withdrawal.

operations.name: core.writeEdgeRoute
operations.description: Write how a connection is drawn on one canvas — its pinned sides and its bends — editing the route, replacing it, making one, or deleting one that says nothing any more.

route.description: The connection’s route on this canvas, where it has one.

fields.description: sourceAnchor, targetAnchor, points — what the route says.

operations.name: feed.reply
operations.description: Answer one line with a typed line of its own: a response to it, threaded under the subject of the thread it is in, mentioning whoever its marks name.

marks.description: Its marks, as the composer gave them; absent when it has none.

thread.description: The subject of the thread it joins.

operations.name: pocket.gather
operations.description: Keep a reference in the Pocket, in a folder or at its root. Something already held is moved to the folder rather than kept twice.

entity.description: The reference’s entity, written out beside it.

withinEntity.description: The record it sits inside, where it is a block.

label.description: How it read when it was gathered.

sourceName.description: The space it came from, by name.

into.description: The folder to keep it in; the root when omitted.

origin.description: Where a row dragged out of the Pocket came from — { id, folder } — so a drop elsewhere moves it.

operations.name: pocket.refile
operations.description: Move an item from one folder to another. The item keeps its id and everything it says, gatheredAt included.

operations.name: pocket.removeFolder
operations.description: Delete a folder, every folder under it at any depth, and everything kept in any of them — the deepest first, so a parent outlives its children.

operations.name: pocket.rootFolder
operations.description: The Pocket’s root folder — the one everything else hangs off — made the first time it is asked for.

operations.name: polls.vote
operations.description: Cast the invoker’s vote on a poll, or change it — one vote per person per poll, any duplicates removed.

option.description: The choice, as it is written in the poll’s options.
